subject.title: [Feature]: Include interaction metadata in Discord button callbacks

question: Should generic Discord component clicks expose a new agent-visible structured interaction metadata envelope, and which fields should be public versus plugin-only?
rationale: The change would alter the public agent inbound context and expose Discord identifiers/callback data, so maintainers need to choose the schema, compatibility shape, and trust boundary before implementation.

options.title: Add Typed Agent Metadata
options.body: Expose a narrow documented envelope with message id, action kind, safe callback/custom data, label/value details, and clicker identity, backed by Discord plugin tests.

options.title: Keep Rich Metadata Plugin-Only
options.body: Leave structured interaction fields on the plugin interactive-handler API and document generic agent fallback callbacks as text-only messages.

options.title: Ship Sender/Message First
options.body: Expose only clicker and originating message ids initially, then defer callback payload semantics to the broader inbound metadata design.

recommendation.title: Add Typed Agent Metadata
recommendation.body: Expose a narrow documented envelope with message id, action kind, safe callback/custom data, label/value details, and clicker identity, backed by Discord plugin tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the broadest recent history across the Discord component, plugin/channel boundary, and session/context surfaces involved in the decision.
